claims.note: The chapter gives no identity link between the BC 109 commissioner and the Guo Chang active in the Dijie era roughly forty years later.
Both local records refer to Great Yu; the split is retained only to preserve stable local IDs.
Independent witnesses and the known Lidui place-name identify the latter as a digital-text corruption.
The received verse reads saline soil and rice-and-millet; both corrupt glyphs were repaired.
The received Hanshu reading denotes saline land.
The Hanshu source form reflects the Zhuang/Yan taboo substitution and omits the final character preserved in Shiji.
Independent witnesses preserve the ordinary ridge graph 嶺.
The vessel counter is 艘; 馏 is a digital-text corruption.
The contrast with 遠者 requires 近者, as independent witnesses confirm.
Independent witnesses identify non-glutinous rice, 粳稻.

translationRepairs: Thereupon Shi Qi was made magistrate of Ye, and he diverted Zhang River water to irrigate Ye, enriching Wei's Henan region.
Thereupon Shi Qi was made magistrate of Ye, and he diverted Zhang River water to irrigate Ye, enriching Wei's Henei region.
The Chinese has 河內, the region/commandery name Henei, not 河南 (Henan); the proposed literal correctly restores that placename.
The emperor agreed, ordered the Qi water engineer Xu Bo to present a memorial, and mobilized tens of thousands. The canal was completed in three years.
The emperor agreed, ordered the Qi water engineer Xu Bo to survey and mark the route, and mobilized tens of thousands. The canal was completed in three years.
In 令齊人水工徐伯表, 表 is the hydraulic verb to survey and stake the canal line, not to present a memorial; the replacement matches that sense and keeps the rest of the sentence intact.
Du Qin advised General-in-chief Wang Feng: "At the previous breach, chancellor's clerk Yang Yan said Yanshi used Yan's method to block it and concealed refusing to see him.

Du Qin advised Grand General Wang Feng: "During the previous breach, Chancellor's Clerk Yang Yan said that Yanshi had used a technique learned from him to close it, but Yanshi suppressed his claim and refused to see him.

蔽不肯見 means Yanshi suppressed Yang Yan's claim and refused to receive him. The original is ungrammatical, while the draft repair leaves the subject of both verbs unclear; the revision restores the names and agency explicitly.
From Henan northward to Liyang, stone embankments forced the river eastward toward Pinggang in Dong Commandery;
From Henei northward to Liyang, stone embankments forced the river eastward toward Pinggang in Dong Commandery;
河從河內北至黎陽 names Henei, not Henan; the idiomatic repair corrects that placename error.
From Henan north to Liyang, stone dikes forced the river east to strike Pinggang in Dong Commandery;
From Henei north to Liyang, stone dikes forced the river east to strike Pinggang in Dong Commandery;
The same 河內 in s0209 is Henei; the literal line must not read Henan, and the proposed replacement is exact.
One should each follow water's nature and no longer irrigate; then all rivers flow freely, channels benefit themselves, and there will be no overflow-breach harm."
Each should be allowed to follow its nature, and irrigation should cease; then all rivers will flow freely, channels will benefit themselves, and there will be no overflow-breach harm."
可各順從其性 needs a distributive "each" subject; "One should each follow" is ungrammatical, and the proposed literal restores that sense plus 毋復灌溉 without adding extraneous meaning.
Chief clerk Wang Heng objected: "The river empties into Bohai, but Bohai terrain is actually higher than Han Mu's proposed cuts.
Clerk to the Grand Minister of Works Wang Heng said: "The river empties into Bohai, but Bohai terrain is actually higher than Han Mu's proposed cuts.
大司空掾 is a clerk attached to the Grand Minister of Works, not a chief clerk, and 言 is neutral "said." The revision restores the full office without promoting Wang Heng beyond the Chinese.
In Shu, Governor Li Bing cut through the Dui Dike to avoid the harm of the Mo River and opened two channels through Chengdu.
In Shu, Administrator Li Bing cut through Lidui to avoid the harm of the Mo River and opened two channels through Chengdu.
Restores the Lidui place-name and identifies the feature as the rock spur cut by Li Bing, not a supposed Dui Dike.
In Shu, Governor Li Bing cut through the Dui Dike to avert Mo River flooding and split the flow into two channels through Chengdu.
In Shu, Administrator Li Bing cut through the Lidui rock spur to avert flooding from the Mo River and opened two channels through Chengdu.
Restores the Lidui place-name and identifies the feature as the rock spur cut by Li Bing, not a supposed Dui Dike.
The people sang: "Ye has a worthy magistrate, Lord Shi; he opened Zhang waters and irrigated Ye's outskirts; through all ages salty wasteland grows rice and millet."
The people sang: "Ye has a worthy magistrate in Lord Shi; he opened the Zhang waters to irrigate the outskirts of Ye; saline waste from time immemorial now grows rice and millet."
Restores the received song reading and gives the verse clearer, more natural English.
People praised him in song: "Ye found a worthy magistrate in Lord Shi; he cut the Zhang to water the fields, and the old saline flats now yield grain forever."
The people sang: "Worthy Lord Shi governs Ye; he opened the Zhang to water its fields, and age-old salt flats now bear rice and millet."
Restores the received song reading and gives the verse clearer, more natural English.
When the canal was completed, it was used to irrigate and drain stagnant waters, irrigating over 40,000 qing of saline land, with yields all of one zhong per mu.
When the canal was completed, its silt-laden water irrigated more than 40,000 qing of saline land, all yielding one zhong per mu.
Corrects the irrigation mechanism: the canal carried fertile silt rather than draining stagnant tracts.
After completion, the canal both irrigated and drained low stagnant tracts, reclaiming over 40,000 qing of salty soil, with yields reaching one zhong per mu.
Once complete, the canal carried fertile silt onto more than 40,000 qing of salt-affected land, raising yields to one zhong per mu.
Corrects the irrigation mechanism: the canal carried fertile silt rather than draining stagnant tracts.
Later Yan Xiong said: "People of Linjin wish to cut a Luo canal to irrigate over 10,000 qing of formerly bad land east of Chongquan.
Later Zhuang Xiongpi said: "The people of Linjin wish to cut a canal from the Luo to irrigate more than 10,000 qing of poor land east of Chongquan.
Identifies the taboo-altered and abbreviated Hanshu name as Zhuang Xiongpi, matching the Shiji parallel.
Later Yan Xiong reported: "People in Linjin request a Luo diversion canal to irrigate more than 10,000 qing of poor land east of Chongquan.
Later Zhuang Xiongpi reported: "The people of Linjin ask to divert the Luo through a canal and irrigate more than 10,000 qing of poor land east of Chongquan.
Identifies the taboo-altered and abbreviated Hanshu name as Zhuang Xiongpi, matching the Shiji parallel.
The water cut through to sever Shangyan, over more than ten li east to the mountain ridge.
The water descended through the shafts to pass beneath Shangyan, across a stretch of more than ten li eastward to the mountain ridge.
Clarifies that water descended through linked shafts to pass beneath Shangyan.
The channel cut through beneath Shangyan and ran eastward for over ten li toward the ridge.
Water descended through the linked shafts and passed beneath Shangyan for more than ten li, as far as the ridge to the east.
Clarifies that water descended through linked shafts to pass beneath Shangyan.
They dispatched inspection and judged the overflow came from Tunshi River; current budget was insufficient, so for now it should not be dredged.
Xu Shang was sent to inspect and judged that the problem had been caused by the Tunshi River overflowing; because current funds were insufficient, dredging could be deferred for the time being.
Restores Xu Shang as the inspector and identifies overflow from the Tunshi River as his diagnosis.
After field inspection, they concluded the flooding stemmed from Tunshi conditions, but current funds were inadequate, so dredging should be deferred.
After inspecting the site, Xu Shang concluded that overflow from the Tunshi River had caused the problem. Since funds were short, he recommended postponing the dredging.
Restores Xu Shang as the inspector and identifies overflow from the Tunshi River as his diagnosis.
River-dike envoy Wang Yanshi was ordered to close the breach, using bamboo fascines four zhang long and nine-chi circumference, filled with small stones, lowered between two boats clamping them.

River-Dike Commissioner Wang Yanshi was ordered to close the breach with bamboo gabions four zhang long and nine arm-spans in circumference, filled with small stones and lowered between two supporting boats.
Corrects 九圍 from nine chi to nine arm-spans in circumference and clarifies how the gabions were lowered.
Dike commissioner Wang Yanshi sealed the breach using bamboo gabions four zhang long and nine chi around, packed with stone and lowered between paired boats.
Dike commissioner Wang Yanshi sealed the breach with stone-filled bamboo gabions four zhang long and nine arm-spans around, lowering them into place between paired boats.
Corrects 九圍 from nine chi to nine arm-spans in circumference and clarifies how the gabions were lowered.
Yang Yan, and Minister of Works Xu Shang, and Remonstrance Grandee Chengma Yannian should be sent to work jointly.
Yang Yan, Superintendent of Imperial Works Xu Shang, and Remonstrance Grandee Chengma Yannian should be sent to work jointly.
Corrects 將作大匠 from Minister of Works to Superintendent of Imperial Works.
Yang Yan should be sent together with Minister of Works Xu Shang and Remonstrance Grandee Chengma Yannian to work jointly.
Yang Yan should be sent to work jointly with Xu Shang, superintendent of imperial works, and Chengma Yannian, grandee of remonstrance.
Corrects 將作大匠 from Minister of Works to Superintendent of Imperial Works.

At that time Li Xun and Xie Guang also said: "When yin qi is excessive, waters grow. Therefore within one day, daytime decreases and nighttime increases; rivers overflow. What is called water not moistening downward: though it normally is in low terrain, still sun and moon changes appear at new and full, showing Heaven's way acts with causes.

At that time Li Xun and Xie Guang also said: "When yin qi flourishes, water rises with it. Thus, within a single day, the water declines by day and increases by night until the rivers overflow. This is what is meant by 'water does not moisten downward.' Although water normally occupies low ground, its changes still appear with those of the sun and moon at the new and full moons, making clear that Heaven's way acts from definite causes.
Clarifies that water levels fell by day and rose by night and preserves the argument linking those changes to lunar phases.

At the same time, Li Xun and Xie Guang said, "When yin force becomes excessive, water rises. That is why within a single day decline by day and increase by night can be observed, and rivers overflow. So-called failure of water to flow down follows celestial causation: signs appear with new and full moons, showing Heaven acts through definite causes.

At the same time, Li Xun and Xie Guang argued: "When yin energy grows too strong, the water rises with it. Within a single day its level falls by daylight and climbs at night until the rivers overflow. This is the portent called 'water failing to flow downward.' Water may normally seek low ground, but its changes still follow the sun and moon at the new and full moons, proof that Heaven's way acts through definite causes.
Clarifies that water levels fell by day and rose by night and preserves the argument linking those changes to lunar phases.

The matter was sent to Chancellor Kong Guang and Grand Minister of Works He Wu, who requested provincial inspectors and administrators of Sanfu, Sanhe, and Hongnong to recommend capable officials and commoners, but none responded to the call.

The matter was sent to Chancellor Kong Guang and Grand Minister of Works He Wu, who requested that regional inspectors and the administrators of the Three Capital Districts, the Three Rivers commanderies, and Hongnong recommend capable officials or commoners, but no one answered the call.
Corrects 三河 to the Three Rivers commanderies and renders the administrative jurisdictions clearly.

The matter was sent down to Chancellor Kong Guang and Grand Minister of Works He Wu, who requested that provincial inspectors and the governors of the Three Adjuncts, the Three Henei commanderies, and Hongnong recommend capable officials and commoners, but no one responded to the order.

The matter went to Chancellor Kong Guang and Grand Minister of Works He Wu. They asked regional inspectors and the governors of the Three Capital Districts, the Three Rivers commanderies, and Hongnong to nominate capable officials or commoners, but no one responded.
Corrects 三河 to the Three Rivers commanderies and renders the administrative jurisdictions clearly.
Thus planting millet and wheat, and also lowland rice, yields fivefold on high fields and tenfold on low fields;
Thus land now planted with millet and wheat could instead grow non-glutinous rice, yielding fivefold on high fields and tenfold on low fields;
Restores 粳稻 and correctly contrasts existing millet and wheat with replacement rice cultivation.
Then wheat and millet yields rise sharply, and paddy cultivation becomes possible - roughly fivefold returns on uplands and tenfold on low fields.
Fields now sown with millet and wheat could instead produce rice, with fivefold returns on higher ground and tenfold on low ground.
Restores 粳稻 and correctly contrasts existing millet and wheat with replacement rice cultivation.
